newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump as political concerns fade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump as political concerns fade.

text.p: Istanbul shares jumped an average 3.93 percent despite profit-taking on Monday as the market brushed aside political worries, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed up 61 points, or 3.93 percent at 1,613, but down from a morning high of 1,620.
It had lost 6.2 percent last week amid fears of a rift in the Islamist-led coalition following the secularist military's demand to fight rising Islamist zeal.
Trade volume rose to 26.06 trillion lira from 21.83 trillion on Friday.

Brokers said hopes that today's National Security Council (MGK) meeting would not cover sensitive issues fuelled purchases at the opening and activity continued until the close despite some afternoon selling.
In line with previous expectations, none of the disputed issues came up at the military-dominated MGK's meeting.

Political concerns had mounted last week due to the ruling Islamist Welfare Party's opposition to a plan to raise compulsory education to eight years from five as part of the measures put forward at the MGK's February 28 meeting.
"The market targets 1,650 levels after establishing a firm base at between 1,600-1,625 with strong volume," said Cem Baycan from Delta securities.
Other brokers said the market would also watch results of an IMF team visit to Turkey this week for an annual review of the economy and March inflation data due to be released on April 4.

Of the 241 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 199 to 19 and 23 were steady. The IMKB Industrial gained 3.16 percent to 1,602, the IMKB Services jumped 4.24 percent to 1,451 and the IMKB Financial leapt 4.55 percent to 1,769.
Top actives were T.Isbank's C series, up 3,000 lira at 50,000 and Ihlas Holding, up 3,750 lira at 25,750. They made up 20 percent of the total turnover.
